title: The Place That Has Never Been Wounded
Years
description: YEARS is a collection of left-field electronica originally written for SOVRN: X, a 14-minute, visually driven skate film blending skating, animation, and photography. The music, composed and produced by Joaquin Pastor and Patrick Logothetti of James Supercave, emerged from their long-running creative relationship with SOVRN’s creative director, Alexandre Souêtre.

As James Supercave, Pastor and Logothetti - alongside bandmate Andrés Villalobos - have spent over a decade shaping a distinct voice in indie and alternative pop, releasing multiple EPs and two full-length albums, touring extensively across North America with artists such as Warpaint, Crystal Castles, and Jungle, and music placements across film, television, and global brand campaigns. That same instinct for melody, texture, and emotional pacing quietly underpins YEARS, even as it moves further into experimental terrain.

Souêtre has shaped the visual identity of their work since the beginning, and the aesthetic and sonic language between these collaborators has grown into something instinctive, almost familial. With no pressure to meet a deadline, both the film and this record were allowed to unfold in their own time. Ideas accumulated, shifted, disappeared, resurfaced. These tracks are the ones that made the cut.

title: Haunted Memory Boy
description: Composed, performed and produced by Kjartan Holm, Francesco Fabris, Sin Fang.
Recorded at INNI Music and Greenhouse Studios, Reykjavík, Iceland. Mixed and mastered by Francesco Fabris.

String quartet in “Haunted Memory Boy” and “Primal Fall”: Pétur Björnsson, Guðbjörg Hlín Guðmundsdóttir (violins), Karl Petska (viola), Unnur Jónsdóttir (cello). Solo violin in “Primal Fall” by Isaac Pross.
Artwork by Ingibjörg Birgisdóttir. Artist photo by Lilja Birgisdóttir.

title: Lucid Distance
description: Lucid Distance is a personal exploration of Hamilton-Ayres’ battle with a desire for escapism, feeling distant and removed from the world. Through what she retrospectively realised was a tumultuous combination of an artist friend’s suicide, prenatal hormones and depression - on wild rollercoaster of emotions, Hamilton-Ayres found herself five months pregnant recording at the European Space Agency’s Large European Acoustic Facility in Winter early 2024.

“Something about being isolated and closed in this massive chamber saturated in sound, two heartbeats, got me thinking about the journey from being encapsulated in the womb and transitioning into the world. A lot of this time writing I was coming to terms with upcoming motherhood.”

It was hearing that other heartbeat that spurred Hamilton-Ayres back into writing. Just as Play Echoes contains an intimate conversation of Hamilton-Ayres as a child talking to her mother, Lucid Distance opens with the heartbeat of her daughter, recorded during a midwife appointment.

title: Stages of Changed
description: To mark the one-year anniversary of Jakob Lindhagen’s Stages of Change — a richly textured audiovisual EP built around a single evolving theme — we’re thrilled to share Stages of Changed, a reimagined take from Swedish electronic duo Dött ljus (Petter Lindhagen & Johan Kisro).

Rather than remix a single track, Dött ljus were given access to every sound from the original EP — approaching it not as six songs, but as one continuous piece to be deconstructed and reshaped. The result is two stunning new tracks: one slow and ambient, the other pulsing and rhythmic, both weaving familiar fragments into something entirely new.
A fitting companion to the original work — and a birthday present of sorts — Stages of Changed offers a fresh perspective on a beloved release.

title: Sun Divider
description: The four songs on ‘Sun Divider’ delve deep into the intersection between their respective musical venn diagrams: Atli is a BAFTA-winning, Emmy-nominated modern classical composer and producer who specialises in film and TV soundtracks, while Talos was a renowned singer and producer who has released three albums, including the Choice Music Prize nominated debut, Wild Alee.

Their combined talents perhaps encouraged the pair to explore different corners of their work, resulting in this mesmerising short collection of songs that immediately draws you into their evocative world.
